summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: algorithm analysis with asymptotic notation and recurrences, discrete mathematics (induction, divisibility, gcd, primes, permutations, summations, modular arithmetic at the level of residues), the schoolbook and divide-and-conquer integer arithmetic algorithms, sorting, and the fast Fourier transform as an O(n log n) convolution algorithm. They have taken linear algebra (matrices, linear maps, rank, inverses, vector norms) and complex numbers, and know basic multitape Turing machines and bit-level data representation. They have not studied abstract algebra beyond what the existing concepts give, finite-field linear algebra, tensor products of vector spaces, analytic number theory, or the research literature on fast multiplication.

known.name: Binary representation of integers and radix expansions
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of digits in a fixed base (here 2 or 2^b), with the leftmost digit most significant, and can be padded on the left with zeros to a fixed length.

known.name: Schoolbook arithmetic and carries
known.gloss: Integers are added digit by digit in linear time with carries, multiplied in quadratic time by long multiplication, and divided by long division, all in time polynomial in the bit length.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform and the convolution theorem
known.gloss: The length-2^k discrete Fourier transform can be computed in O(N log N) arithmetic operations by divide and conquer, which makes convolution and hence polynomial or integer multiplication fast.

known.name: Linear maps and matrices
known.gloss: A linear map is represented by a matrix acting on coordinate vectors; matrices have products, inverses when they exist, a rank, and diagonal and identity special cases.

known.name: Vector norms and the triangle inequality
known.gloss: A norm assigns each vector a size (here the largest coordinate modulus) satisfying the triangle inequality ||u+v|| <= ||u|| + ||v||, and a linear map has an induced operator norm equal to the largest ratio ||Lu||/||u||.

known.name: Permutations of indices
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of an index set onto itself, and applying one to a list reorders its entries without changing their values.

known.name: Divisibility, gcd and coprime integers
known.gloss: Integers divide with a quotient and remainder, two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1, and a number coprime to a modulus has an inverse modulo it.

known.name: Prime numbers and primality testing by trial division
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and itself, and one can find or test primes by trial division.

known.name: Floor, ceiling, rounding and logarithms
known.gloss: The floor and ceiling functions round a real number down or up to an integer, and lg x and ln x denote the base-2 and natural logarithms.

known.name: Bitwise XOR and Hamming weight
known.gloss: XOR of two bits is their sum modulo 2, applied coordinatewise to bit strings, and the Hamming weight of a bit string is the number of its 1 bits.

known.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: Theta gives matching upper and lower bounds on growth, Omega gives a lower bound, and little-o means strictly smaller order than the stated function.

known.name: Recurrences, induction and geometric series
known.gloss: Costs of recursive procedures are bounded by solving recurrences by unrolling and summing geometric series, and statements about all stages are proved by induction.

known.name: Sorting and its O(N log N) cost
known.gloss: N records can be put in order of their keys in O(N log N) comparisons, and such sorting can be carried out on Turing machine tapes.

known.name: Summation, product and index notation
known.gloss: Sums and products over index ranges, indicator values in {0,1}, and tuples indexed by Cartesian products of finite sets are the notation used to write arrays and transforms.

known.name: Integers, rationals and Gaussian integers
known.gloss: The integers sit inside the rational numbers and the Gaussian integers a + bi with integer a and b, and dyadic rationals are fractions whose denominator is a power of two.

known.name: Euler's formula and complex exponentials
known.gloss: e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta is a point on the unit circle, so e^{i theta} has modulus one and exponents add when such numbers are multiplied.

known.name: Time and bit complexity of Turing machine computation
known.gloss: Running time is the number of machine steps as a function of input length in the worst case, and on tapes data must be moved by the heads, so rearranging stored data costs time proportional to the distance moved.
